title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up a 'standard presentation' of an equisingular stratification of type I, where I is a finite ordered set. On the previous page (15) this is a contravariant functor Sigma from the poset Drap(I) of flags d = (i0<...<in) of I into a model category M of spaces. Restriction from a flag to an initial segment is a fibration (1). Deleting a non-last element is a 'plongement-bord', i.e. a boundary / cylindrical embedding (2).

This page:

(i) Starred footnote. It suffices to require fibrancy for initial-segment inclusions d subset d' where d contains the largest element of the relevant subflag. Sigma_d -> Sigma_delta is then of the stated type.

(ii) Condition (3), the key condition. Let d and d' be flags with last(d) = first(d') = i, and put d'' = d u d'. The square
  Sigma_{d''} -> Sigma_{d'} (delete the elements of d before i: an embedding)
  Sigma_{d''} -> Sigma_d (restrict to an initial segment: a fibration)
  Sigma_{d'} -> Sigma_i (fibration)
  Sigma_d -> Sigma_i (embedding)
must be cartesian. The condition is vacuous if d or d' has length 0. It suffices to check it for flags of length 2. A right-margin addition requires transversality: the fibration Sigma_{d'} -> Sigma_delta must be transverse to the cylindrical embedding of Sigma_d, compatibly with the cylindrical structures.

(iii) Consequence. Iterating (3) gives Sigma_{i0...in} = Sigma_{i0 i1} x_{Sigma_{i1}} ... x_{Sigma_{i(n-1)}} Sigma_{i(n-1) in}. So the whole functor is recovered, by induction on flag length, from three pieces of data:
- the Sigma_i (strata, 'unfolded' into spaces with boundary or corners);
- the Sigma_ij for i<j, with a fibration Sigma_ij -> Sigma_i (the link bundle) and a boundary embedding Sigma_ij -> Sigma_j (the boundary of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of stratum i inside stratum j);
- composition maps Sigma_ij x_{Sigma_j} Sigma_jk =: Sigma_ijk -> Sigma_ik, subject to conditions (associativity and the like).

(iv) Left margin. It describes the corner structure inside Sigma_j:
- a) faces Sigma_kj and Sigma_lj are disjoint when k and l are incomparable;
- b) Sigma_{i0..in} is the intersection of the faces Sigma_{i0 in}, ..., Sigma_{i(n-1) in};
- c) Sigma_d n Sigma_{d'} = Sigma_{d u d'}, which is empty if d u d' is not a flag.

(v) Next page. All of this is repackaged as a non-unital 'category object' over I: objects Sigma_*, morphisms Sigma_**, a source map that is a fibration, a target map that is a closed immersion, and identities Sigma_ii = Sigma_i.

In modern terms: a functor on sd(I)^op satisfying the Segal condition, with Reedy-type point-set fibrancy and cofibrancy conditions. In other words, a point-set, manifold-with-corners version of the 'décollage' description of an I-stratified space, i.e. the unzipping/déploiement of a stratified space into manifolds with corners glued along link bundles.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The square in (3) is consistent with conditions (1)-(2): its vertical arrows are fibrations and its horizontal arrows are boundary embeddings, so the pullback of an embedding along a fibration makes sense.
Gap: the conditions on the composition maps Sigma_ijk -> Sigma_ik (associativity, compatibility with fibrations and corner structure) are announced but not yet listed on this page.
The transversality requirement is only sketched in the margin. Its precise formulation relative to the 'cylindrical structures' is left unclear.

ideas.what: Stratified space presented as a contravariant functor on the poset of flags of I (the subdivision sd(I)), with initial-segment restrictions as fibrations and face deletions as boundary embeddings
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / resolution of a stratified space into a sd(P)-diagram of manifolds with corners; Reedy-fibrant décollage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom-Mather control data (1969-70), Verona resolution; Ayala-Francis-Tanaka 'unzip' (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches 'déploiement' of tame stratified spaces informally

ideas.what: Cartesian (Segal) condition: Sigma_{d u d'} = Sigma_d x_{Sigma_i} Sigma_{d'} when last(d)=first(d')=i, reducing all data to length <= 2
ideas.modern_name: Segal condition for décollages (functors sd(P)^op -> spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Barwick-Glasman-Haine, 'Exodromy' (2018); Haine, homotopy theory of stratified spaces

ideas.what: Encoding of the data as a non-unital category object over I: objects Sigma_*, morphisms Sigma_**, source a fibration, target a closed embedding, composition Sigma_ij x_{Sigma_j} Sigma_jk -> Sigma_ik
ideas.modern_name: Point-set model of the exit-path category / link category of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit-path infinity-categories); AFT link data

ideas.what: Corner/face incidence conditions in Sigma_j: faces from incomparable strata are disjoint; Sigma_d n Sigma_{d'} = Sigma_{d u d'}

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, around 1981-82, exactly the Segal-type condition that later defines 'décollages' (Barwick-Glasman-Haine). A stratified space over a poset I is given by a functor on flags of I in which the value on a concatenated flag is the fibre product over the junction stratum. Grothendieck adds point-set fibration/cofibration requirements and reconstructs everything from the link bundles Sigma_ij and the compositions Sigma_ijk -> Sigma_ik. This anticipates the décollage/exit-path description of stratified homotopy types, and the AFT unzipping, as a single combinatorial framework.
missed.quote: considérant d'' = d ∪ d' et le diagramme Σ_{d''} ↪ Σ_{d'}, Σ_d ↪ Σ_i ... ce dernier est cartésien ... Il suffit de le vérifier pour d et d' de longueur 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a strict point-set (Reedy-fibrant) model, with cylindrical/transversality conditions, bridging Thom-Mather tame topology and the infinity-categorical décollage/exodromy theory. This could inform a geometric rectification theorem for conically smooth or tame stratified spaces.

missed.claim: Two pieces are left unfinished. First, the conditions on the composition maps Sigma_ij x_{Sigma_j} Sigma_jk -> Sigma_ik. Second, the transversality requirement relating fibrations to cylindrical embeddings. Together these would make the equivalence 'stratified space <-> (Sigma_i, Sigma_ij, compositions)' precise.
missed.quote: il faut se donner les morphismes Σ_ij ×_{Σ_j} Σ_jk → Σ_ik satisfaisant aux conditions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A complete point-set reconstruction theorem of this kind ('déploiement' equivalence) is still not standard outside the smooth/conically smooth setting.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states cleanly the Segal/cartesian condition on flag-indexed diagrams and the 'category object' packaging of link bundles. This is essentially the décollage formalism of Barwick-Glasman-Haine, published decades later without reference to these notes. The general idea of déploiement is hinted at in Esquisse, and Thom-Mather control data are classical, so this is not wholly new.
transcription_corrections: Margin item b) appears to read Σ_{i0…in} = Σ_{i0 in} ∩ … ∩ Σ_{i(n-1) in} (faces inside Σ_{in}), not Σ_{i0 i1} ∩ … ∩ Σ_{i(n-1) in}.
Margin item a) likely reads 'Σ_kj ∩ Σ_lj = ∅ si k, l non comparables'.
'Il suffit de le vérifier pour d et d' de longueur 2' — 'longueur' here probably counts elements (flags (i<j)).
